symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Triangular-array index.

symbols.name: B_n
symbols.def: Number of sequential randomization blocks in array \(n\).

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: Block index.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: Partial-sum time index.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of treatment arms, fixed across the triangular array.

symbols.name: \mathcal A
symbols.def: Set of treatment arms.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Treatment-arm index.

symbols.name: \mathcal U_{nb}
symbols.def: Units entering block \(b\) of array \(n\).

symbols.name: n_{nb}
symbols.def: Block size \(n_{nb}=|\mathcal U_{nb}|\).

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: Unit index within block \(b\).

symbols.name: N_n
symbols.def: Total population size \(N_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: w_{nb}
symbols.def: Block weight \(w_{nb}=n_{nb}/N_n\).

symbols.name: Y_{nbi}(a)
symbols.def: Potential outcome of unit \(i\) in block \(b\) under arm \(a\).

symbols.name: Z_{nbi}
symbols.def: Assigned arm for unit \(i\) in block \(b\).

symbols.name: Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: Observed response \(Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{nbi}(Z_{nbi})\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_{n,b-1}
symbols.def: Pre-block history containing all prior assignments and observed outcomes and the current block's baseline information.

symbols.name: m_{nba}
symbols.def: Number of units assigned to arm \(a\) in block \(b\), with \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}=n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: p_{nba}
symbols.def: Marginal assignment probability \(p_{nba}=m_{nba}/n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Prespecified arm contrast \(c=(c_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}\).

symbols.name: g_{nbi}(a)
symbols.def: Past-fitted prediction for \(Y_{nbi}(a)\), evaluated before block \(b\) is randomized.

symbols.name: R_{nbi}(a)
symbols.def: Residual \(R_{nbi}(a)=Y_{nbi}(a)-g_{nbi}(a)\), fixed conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\).

symbols.name: \bar R_{nba}
symbols.def: Armwise block residual mean \(\bar R_{nba}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}R_{nbi}(a)\).

symbols.name: S_{nba}^2
symbols.def: Residual variance \(S_{nba}^2=(n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\{R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}\}^2\).

symbols.name: \mu_{nba}
symbols.def: Centered residual marginal \(\mu_{nba}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\delta_{R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}}\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_{nb}
symbols.def: Set \(\Gamma(\mu_{nb1},\ldots,\mu_{nbK})\) of probability laws on \(\mathbb R^K\) with the stated armwise marginals.

symbols.name: J_{nb}^{-}
symbols.def: Minimum quadratic contrast cost over \(\Gamma_{nb}\).

symbols.name: J_{nb}^{+}
symbols.def: Maximum quadratic contrast cost over \(\Gamma_{nb}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal O_{nba}
symbols.def: Assigned-arm index set \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\), whose cardinality is \(m_{nba}\) under complete-block randomization.

symbols.name: \widehat{\bar R}_{nba}
symbols.def: Assigned-arm sample mean \(\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)
symbols.def: For \(i\in\mathcal O_{nba}\), the observable centered residual \(\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}\).

symbols.name: \widehat S_{nba}^2
symbols.def: Observable variance \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=(m_{nba}-1)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2\) when \(m_{nba}\ge2\), with value zero when \(m_{nba}\le1\).

symbols.name: \widehat\mu_{nba}
symbols.def: Observable assigned-arm residual measure \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)}\). If \(m_{nba}=0\), set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\).

symbols.name: \widehat J_{nb}^{-}
symbols.def: Minimum empirical transport cost formed from \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\).

symbols.name: \widehat J_{nb}^{+}
symbols.def: Maximum empirical transport cost formed from \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\).

symbols.name: \tau_n
symbols.def: Contrast average \(\tau_n=N_n^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_aY_{nbi}(a)\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_n
symbols.def: Predictably adjusted AIPW estimator of \(\tau_n\).

symbols.name: D_{nb}
symbols.def: Centered block contribution satisfying \(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}D_{nb}\).

symbols.name: M_{nj}
symbols.def: Partial-sum process \(M_{nj}=\sum_{b=1}^{j}D_{nb}\) for \(j\le B_n\).

symbols.name: V_n
symbols.def: Predictable quadratic variation \(V_n=\langle M_n\rangle_{B_n}=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\).
symbols.role: true design variance along the adaptive history

symbols.name: s_n^2
symbols.def: Primitive design scale \(s_n^2=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon_0
symbols.def: Common overlap constant for the uniform triangular-array class.

symbols.name: \delta_0
symbols.def: Common excess-moment exponent for the nuisance-adjusted residual arrays.

symbols.name: C_R
symbols.def: Common \((4+\delta_0)\)-moment envelope for all predictable-adjustment residuals.

symbols.name: q_n
symbols.def: Common lower arm-count sequence satisfying \(q_n/\log(2B_nK)\to\infty\).

symbols.name: \ell_n
symbols.def: Common maximal-block-leverage envelope satisfying \(\ell_n\to0\).

symbols.name: v_0
symbols.def: Common lower predictable-quadratic-variation constant for the uniform class.

symbols.name: r_n
symbols.def: Endpoint-error envelope \(r_n=\{\log(2B_nK)/q_n\}^{\delta_0/[8(4+\delta_0)]}+\ell_n^{\delta_0/[8(4+\delta_0)]}\), which tends to zero.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm{ep}}
symbols.def: A constant depending only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\), whose existence is asserted by \(\text{thm:history-uniform-plugin}\).

symbols.name: L_n
symbols.def: Lower endpoint of the predictable coupling envelope for \(V_n\).

symbols.name: U_n
symbols.def: Upper endpoint of the predictable coupling envelope for \(V_n\).

symbols.name: \widehat L_n
symbols.def: Plug-in lower endpoint formed from observed armwise residual marginals.

symbols.name: \widehat U_n
symbols.def: Plug-in upper endpoint formed from observed armwise residual marginals.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: Nominal error probability.

symbols.name: z_{1-\alpha/2}
symbols.def: The \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).

symbols.name: \mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}
symbols.def: Wald interval centered at \(\widehat\tau_n\) and scaled by \(\widehat U_n\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak D
symbols.def: Uniform class \(\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))\) defined in \(\text{def:admissible-arrays}\).

symbols.name: \gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}
symbols.def: Joint centered residual law induced by the common unit labels in block \(b\) at the realized pre-block history.

symbols.name: \mathcal H_{n,b-1}
symbols.def: Universal tree of assignment prefixes before block \(b\); a fixed potential-outcome completion fills in the observed responses at each prefix and thereby induces the corresponding \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-history, including nodes off the ultimately realized path.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: An assignment-prefix node at which a completion induces observed responses and the prespecified design and fitting rules are evaluated.

symbols.name: g_{nbi}^{h}(a)
symbols.def: Value produced for unit \(i\) and arm \(a\) by the fixed predictable fitting rule when the pre-block history is \(h\).

symbols.name: R_{nbi}^{h}(a)
symbols.def: Residual \(R_{nbi}^{h}(a)=Y_{nbi}(a)-g_{nbi}^{h}(a)\) at history node \(h\).

symbols.name: \bar R_{nba}^{h}
symbols.def: Mean \(\bar R_{nba}^{h}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}R_{nbi}^{h}(a)\).

symbols.name: \mu_{nba}^{h}
symbols.def: Centered empirical marginal of \(R_{nbi}^{h}(a)\) across \(i\in\mathcal U_{nb}\) at node \(h\).

symbols.name: m_{nba}^{h}
symbols.def: Arm-\(a\) count produced by the prespecified predictable allocation rule at node \(h\), with \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}^{h}=n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: (S_{nba}^{h})^2
symbols.def: Finite-population variance of \(R_{nbi}^{h}(a)\) across \(i\in\mathcal U_{nb}\) at node \(h\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_{nb}^{h}
symbols.def: The set \(\Gamma(\mu_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,\mu_{nbK}^{h})\) of convexified joint residual laws at node \(h\).

symbols.name: J_{nb}^{h,-}
symbols.def: Minimum quadratic contrast cost over \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\).

symbols.name: J_{nb}^{h,+}
symbols.def: Maximum quadratic contrast cost over \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\).

symbols.name: \boldsymbol\mu_n
symbols.def: The ex ante collection \(\boldsymbol\mu_n=(\mu_{nba}^{h})_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) indexed by every possible pre-block history.

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
symbols.def: The Cartesian product of \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\) over all blocks and all possible pre-block histories.

symbols.name: \Xi_n
symbols.def: One fixed potential-outcome array together with the evaluations, at every history node, of the prespecified predictable design and fitting rules.

symbols.name: \gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}
symbols.def: The joint coupling induced at node \(h\) by the common unit labels in the single completion \(\Xi_n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
symbols.type: set of ex ante deterministic completion objects
symbols.def: History-tree compatible fixed-potential-outcome completions defined in \(\text{def:completion-class}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal P_n
symbols.type: finite set of root-to-leaf assignment paths
symbols.def: Set of complete assignment paths through the universal history tree.

symbols.name: \varpi
symbols.def: A complete assignment path through the history tree.

symbols.name: h_b(\varpi)
symbols.def: The pre-block node visited by path \(\varpi\) before block \(b\).

symbols.name: U_{nb}^{h}
symbols.def: Nodewise upper conditional-variance contribution \(U_{nb}^{h}=w_{nb}^2\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a^2(S_{nba}^{h})^2/m_{nba}^{h}-J_{nb}^{h,-}/(n_{nb}-1)\}\), with the variances and predictable counts evaluated at \(h\).

symbols.name: Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}
symbols.def: Conditional-variance contribution \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}=w_{nb}^2\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a^2(S_{nba}^{h})^2/m_{nba}^{h}-(n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\int(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\}\) induced by completion \(\Xi_n\) at node \(h\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{nb}^{h}
symbols.type: finite set of deterministic nodewise couplings
symbols.def: Couplings of \(\mu_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,\mu_{nbK}^{h}\) induced by same-size unit-label matchings at node \(h\), ignoring compatibility with other history nodes.

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.def: Fixed fractional reduction applied to every nodewise rectangular upper contribution.

symbols.name: U_{nb}^{h,\rho}
symbols.def: Fixed-fraction nodewise reduction \(U_{nb}^{h,\rho}=(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h}\).

symbols.name: U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)
symbols.def: Reduced pathwise endpoint \(U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}\).

symbols.name: \Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
symbols.def: Normalized global compatibility gap defined in \(\text{def:completion-gap}\).

symbols.name: \Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
symbols.def: Normalized worst single-node multi-index integrality gap defined in \(\text{def:completion-gap}\).

assumptions.condition: Conditional on baseline information, the array \(\{Y_{nbi}(a):b\le B_n,\ i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\ a\in\mathcal A\}\) is nonrandom under the assignment law.
The fixed-count vector \((m_{nba})_{a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).

novel.justification: This is an explicit fixed-count complete-block design restriction of the paper. It is implementable in predictably batched platform experiments that update integer arm quotas after each completed batch and then use uniform complete randomization within the next batch; minimum cell sizes and capacity caps can be enforced directly by the quota rule. Li and Zhao's broader block-adaptive framework is not cited as supplying this restriction.

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), \((Z_{nbi})_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\) is uniform over assignments having exactly \(m_{nba}\) units in every arm \(a\in\mathcal A\).

standard.name: Complete randomization within a predictable block

assumptions.condition: The array \((g_{nbi}(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
The predictable arm fractions satisfy \(\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0\) almost surely for every \(n\), \(b\), and \(a\).
The predictable counts satisfy \(\min_{b\le B_n,\,a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) almost surely for every \(n\).
The design leverage satisfies \(\max_{b\le B_n}\{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\}/s_n^2\le\ell_n\) for every \(n\).
The nuisance-adjusted residual arrays satisfy \(\sup_{n,b,a}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\le C_R\).
The predictable quadratic variation satisfies \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\) almost surely for every \(n\).

novel.justification: This common finite-population condition excludes asymptotically deterministic contrasts while allowing heterogeneous residual couplings; it holds, for example, when each root-to-leaf path contains a fixed share of blocks with residual contrast variance bounded below relative to \(s_n^2\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(\eta>0\), the predictable quadratic variation stabilizes at its deterministic design expectation uniformly over the common-parameter class: \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left(\left|\frac{V_n}{E_{\mathbb D}V_n}-1\right|>\eta\right)\longrightarrow0.\]

novel.justification: standard: predictable-variation stabilization for a martingale triangular array

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))=\left\{(Y_{nbi}(a),Z_{nbi},m_{nba},g_{nbi}(a))_{n\ge1,\,b\le B_n,\,i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}:\begin{array}{l}K\text{ is fixed, and every member-property assumption listed below holds for all }n;\\ \varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)\text{ are the same displayed constants and deterministic envelopes for every array}\end{array}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \(\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a),\widehat S_{nba}^2,\widehat\mu_{nba}\)
definitions.construction: For \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\) of observed size \(|\mathcal O_{nba}|=m_{nba}\), define \[\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\},\qquad \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},\] \[\widehat\mu_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)},\qquad \widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac1{m_{nba}-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2.\] Set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) and \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=0\), and set \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=1\). These total conventions are inactive for the endpoint theorem for all sufficiently large \(n\), because \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) and \(q_n/\log(2B_nK)\to\infty\).

definitions.name: \([\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\)
definitions.construction: Using only the assigned-arm measures and sample variances from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\), define \[\widehat L_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{+}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\qquad \widehat U_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Two-arm sorting map
definitions.construction: For \(K=2\) and \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), let \(F_{nb,a}^{-1}\) be the quantile function of \(\mu_{nba}\) and compute \[J_{nb}^{-}=\frac12\int_0^1\{F_{nb,1}^{-1}(u)-F_{nb,2}^{-1}(u)\}^2\,du,\qquad J_{nb}^{+}=\frac12\int_0^1\{F_{nb,1}^{-1}(u)-F_{nb,2}^{-1}(1-u)\}^2\,du.\]

definitions.name: Fixed-\(K\) empirical transportation program
definitions.construction: Feed the observable measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)}\) from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\) into the finite program. When every \(m_{nba}>0\), optimize over variables \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\), indexed by \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\), the objective \[\sum_{i_1\in\mathcal O_{nb1}}\cdots\sum_{i_K\in\mathcal O_{nbK}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\left\{\sum_{a=1}^Kc_a\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)\right\}^2\] subject, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\), to the exact marginal constraints \[\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}.\] The minimum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and the maximum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\). If an arm sample is empty, represent its convention \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) by one artificial zero atom of mass one and solve the same marginal-coupling program; the admissible class never invokes this branch.

definitions.name: Worked validation: the \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\) coupling witness
definitions.construction: Take one block of size \(n_{nb}=4\), \(K=2\), the unnormalized contrast \(c=(1,-1)\), and both centered marginal lists equal to \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\). Direct substitution into the two-arm sorting costs gives \[J_{nb}^{-}=\frac14\{(-1+1)^2+(-1+1)^2+(1-1)^2+(1-1)^2\}=0\] under equal-rank pairing and \[J_{nb}^{+}=\frac14\{(-1-1)^2+(-1-1)^2+(1+1)^2+(1+1)^2\}=4\] under reverse-rank pairing. Substitution into \(\text{def:qv-envelope}\) therefore gives \(U_n-L_n=w_{nb}^2(J_{nb}^{+}-J_{nb}^{-})/(n_{nb}-1)=4w_{nb}^2/3>0\) for this single block. Under the normalized contrast \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), both costs and the width are divided by two. This is a direct arithmetic validation of sorting direction and endpoint signs, not a theorem contribution.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\)
definitions.construction: For the ex ante history-tree margin system \(\boldsymbol\mu_n=(\mu_{nba}^{h})_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\,a\in\mathcal A}\), set \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}=\Gamma(\mu_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,\mu_{nbK}^{h})\), define \[J_{nb}^{h,-}=\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}}\int(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a)^2d\gamma,\qquad J_{nb}^{h,+}=\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}}\int(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a)^2d\gamma,\] define \[U_{nb}^{h}=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2(S_{nba}^{h})^2}{m_{nba}^{h}}-\frac{J_{nb}^{h,-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\] and let \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\prod_{b=1}^{B_n}\prod_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}}\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\). The Cartesian product permits a separate convexified coupling at every history node.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\left\{\Xi_n=\left((Y_{nbi}(a))_{b,i,a},(m_{nba}^{h})_{b,h,a},(g_{nbi}^{h}(a))_{b,h,i,a}\right):\begin{array}{l}(Y_{nbi}(a))_{b,i,a}\text{ is fixed before randomization};\\ (m_{nba}^{h})_{a\in\mathcal A}\text{ and }(g_{nbi}^{h}(a))_{i,a}\text{ are the evaluations of the same prespecified predictable allocation and fitting rules at every }h;\\ \text{for every }b\le B_n\text{ and }h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\ R_{nbi}^{h}(a)=Y_{nbi}(a)-g_{nbi}^{h}(a)\text{ has centered margins }\mu_{nba}^{h};\\ \gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\delta_{(R_{nbi}^{h}(1)-\bar R_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,R_{nbi}^{h}(K)-\bar R_{nbK}^{h})}\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\end{array}\right\}.\] Thus one member fixes common unit labels and all potential outcomes before assignment and induces the counts, fitted values, residual margins, feasible couplings, and transport endpoints at every node, including nodes off the realized path.

definitions.name: \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n),\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n),U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)\)
definitions.construction: For \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), let \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\) be its nodewise conditional-variance contribution. With the predictable block weight already included in \(U_{nb}^{h}\) and \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\), define the normalized root-to-leaf compatibility gap \[\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}\ \sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}\frac1{s_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\left\{U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}-Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}\right\}.\] Define the single-node multi-index integrality diagnostic \[\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\sup_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}\left[\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma-J_{nb}^{h,-}\right].\] For a fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\), define the reduced nodewise contribution \(U_{nb}^{h,\rho}=(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h}\) and the corresponding root-to-leaf endpoint \[U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi),\rho}.\]

definitions.name: History-tree integer-flow handle
definitions.construction: Represent one ex ante sequence \((\Xi_n)_{n\ge1}\), with \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) and its entire induced triangular experiment-analysis array in \(\mathfrak D\), as a history-tree integer multi-index flow with common unit labels. Enforce prefix consistency by backward induction and compare its root-to-leaf objective with \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\). Use rational replication at an isolated node to measure \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), then identify the additional loss caused by sharing one potential-outcome array and one fitting rule across incompatible branches while preserving membership in \(\mathfrak D\).

statements.statement: For every array in \(\mathfrak D\), \((M_{nj},\mathcal F_{n,j})_{j\le B_n}\) is a martingale and \[E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac1{n_{nb}-1}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\right\},\] where \(\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\in\Gamma_{nb}\) is the joint centered residual coupling in block \(b\). At every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}\), the conditional variance range over \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\) has endpoints obtained from \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\) and \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\), and both endpoints are attained in that node's convexified coupling set. Evaluating these nodewise endpoints along the realized pre-block histories yields the predictable pathwise containment \(V_n\in[L_n,U_n]\). The interval is exact in the rectangular convexified history-tree relaxation \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\); this theorem does not assert that one \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) simultaneously realizes the selected optimizers across the tree. When \(B_n=1\) and \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), the result reduces to the static quadratic MOT variance formula of Gao, Ge, and Qian. When \(B_n\ge2\) and counts respond to earlier outcomes, \([L_n,U_n]\) is a sum of pre-block-measurable random endpoints rather than one static MOT functional, and the claim does not condition on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\).

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and a block \(b\), and abbreviate \(N=n_{nb}\), \(m_a=m_{nba}\), \(p_a=m_a/N\), \(R_i(a)=R_{nbi}(a)\), and \(x_i(a)=R_i(a)-\bar R_{nba}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\text{-}potential\text{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:predictable\text{-}adjustment}\), all the \(x_i(a)\)'s are fixed conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:predictable\text{-}counts}\), so are the positive integers \(m_a\).  Finally, \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}block\text{-}randomization}\) gives
\[
 E\{\mathbf 1(Z_{nbi}=a)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}=\frac{m_a}{N}=p_a.
\]
Consequently the arm sample mean is conditionally unbiased for its finite-population mean, and the definition in \(\mathrm{def:block\text{-}martingale}\) gives
\[
 E(D_{nb}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
 =w_{nb}\sum_a c_a\left\{m_a^{-1}\sum_i p_aR_i(a)-\bar R_{nba}\right\}=0.
\]
Thus \(M_{nj}=\sum_{b\le j}D_{nb}\) is adapted, integrable, and has zero conditional increments; it is a martingale.

We next calculate its conditional variance.  Complete randomization gives, for distinct units \(i\ne k\),
\[
 E(I_i^aI_k^a\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=\frac{m_a(m_a-1)}{N(N-1)},
 \qquad
 E(I_i^aI_k^{a'}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=\frac{m_am_{a'}}{N(N-1)}\quad(a\ne a'),
\]
where \(I_i^a=\mathbf 1(Z_{nbi}=a)\), while \(I_i^aI_i^{a'}=0\) for \(a\ne a'\).  Expanding the two sample means and using \(\sum_i x_i(a)=0\) therefore yields
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(m_a^{-1}\sum_iI_i^aR_i(a)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)
 =\left(\frac1{m_a}-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2
\]
and, for \(a\ne a'\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(m_a^{-1}\sum_iI_i^aR_i(a),m_{a'}^{-1}\sum_iI_i^{a'}R_i(a')\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)
 =-\frac{S_{nb,aa'}}N,
\]
where
\[
 S_{nb,aa'}=\frac1{N-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}x_i(a)x_i(a').
\]
It follows equation by equation that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})/w_{nb}^2
 &=\sum_a c_a^2\frac{S_{nba}^2}{m_a}
   -\frac1N\left\{\sum_a c_a^2S_{nba}^2+2\sum_{a<a'}c_ac_{a'}S_{nb,aa'}\right\}\\
 &=\sum_a c_a^2\frac{S_{nba}^2}{m_a}
   -\frac1{N(N-1)}\sum_i\left\{\sum_ac_ax_i(a)\right\}^2\\
 &=\sum_a c_a^2\frac{S_{nba}^2}{m_a}
   -\frac1{N-1}\int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The last equality uses the definition
\(\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{(x_i(1),\ldots,x_i(K))}\), whose \(a\)-th marginal is exactly \(\mu_{nba}\); hence \(\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\in\Gamma_{nb}\).

At a fixed history node \(h\), every margin has finite support, so \(\Gamma_{nb}^h\) is a nonempty compact finite-dimensional transportation polytope.  The displayed quadratic cost is a linear continuous functional of its coupling variable.  It therefore attains its minimum \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\) and maximum \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\), and convexity shows that its image is the whole interval between them.  Since the cost enters the conditional variance with coefficient \(-w_{nb}^2/(n_{nb}-1)\), the variance range has lower endpoint obtained from \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\) and upper endpoint obtained from \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\).  Nonnegativity also follows directly from
\[
 \left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2
 =\left(\sum_a\frac{c_ax_a}{\sqrt{p_{nba}}}\sqrt{p_{nba}}\right)^2
 \le\sum_a\frac{c_a^2x_a^2}{p_{nba}},
\]
because \(\sum_ap_{nba}=1\) and
\(\int x_a^2d\mu_{nba}=(n_{nb}-1)S_{nba}^2/n_{nb}\).

The product in \(\mathrm{def:history\text{-}tree\text{-}rectangular\text{-}relaxation}\) permits the coupling to be chosen independently at each node.  On any root-to-leaf path, summing the nodewise intervals gives precisely the interval whose endpoints are the corresponding sums, because a Minkowski sum of real intervals is an interval.  On the realized path the true nodewise coupling is feasible at every visited node, so summing the conditional variances gives \(V_n\in[L_n,U_n]\) pathwise.  Every summand is measurable before its block is randomized; no conditioning on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\) has been used.  This proves exactness in \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), while \(\mathrm{def:completion\text{-}class}\) explains why it makes no assertion of simultaneous attainment by one \(\Xi_n\).

For the two-block kill test, the same conditional-centering calculation gives
\[
 E(D_{n1}D_{n2})=E\{D_{n1}E(D_{n2}\mid\mathcal F_{n,1})\}=0
\]
for every first-block assignment prefix, even when the second count vector is an arbitrary \(\mathcal F_{n,1}\)-measurable function of the first-block assignments and outcomes.  Hence no unidentified cross-block covariance survives.  Finally, when \(B_n=1\) and \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), the residuals are the potential outcomes and direct substitution gives the stated static quadratic multi-marginal transport variance formula.

statements.statement: For \(B_n=2\), let the second-block count vector be any \(\mathcal F_{n,1}\)-measurable function of first-block assignments and outcomes. Then \(E(D_{n1})=0\), \(E(D_{n2}\mid\mathcal F_{n,1})=0\), \(E(D_{n1}D_{n2})=0\), and \(V_n=E(D_{n1}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,0})+E(D_{n2}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,1})\). Enumerating a four-unit two-arm example with first-block counts \((2,2)\) and second-block counts switching between \((1,3)\) and \((3,1)\) confirms that the total variance equals the sum of the two conditional variances for every first-block history.
statements.justification: This is the early falsification check: any surviving cross-block covariance would destroy the blockwise transport reduction.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) with \(B_n=2\).  We first prove the assertions without specializing the block sizes.  Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), the count vector is fixed by \(\mathrm{ass{:}predictable\text{-}counts}\), the adjustment array is fixed by \(\mathrm{ass{:}predictable\text{-}adjustment}\), and the potential-outcome array is fixed by the design-based definition of \(Y_{nbi}(a)\).  Hence every \(R_{nbi}(a)\) and \(\bar R_{nba}\) is fixed under this conditioning.  The positivity built into the declared range \(m_{nba}\in\{1,\ldots,n_{nb}-1\}\) makes all sample-mean divisions below legitimate.

Write \(I_{nbi}(a)=\mathbf 1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}\).  Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}complete\text{-}block\text{-}randomization}\), the number of assignments in the conditional support is
\[
 \frac{n_{nb}!}{\prod_{d\in\mathcal A}m_{nbd}!},
\]
whereas the number assigning a fixed unit \(i\) to arm \(a\) is
\[
 \frac{(n_{nb}-1)!}{(m_{nba}-1)!\prod_{d\ne a}m_{nbd}!}.
\]
Their ratio gives the conditional first-order inclusion probability
\[
 \Pr\{Z_{nbi}=a\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}=\frac{m_{nba}}{n_{nb}}=p_{nba}.
\]
Linearity over the finite conditional assignment support therefore yields, arm by arm,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E\!\left[
   \frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}I_{nbi}(a)R_{nbi}(a)
   \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal F_{n,b-1}
 \right]
 &=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}
   \frac{m_{nba}}{n_{nb}}R_{nbi}(a)\\
 &=\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}R_{nbi}(a)
 =\bar R_{nba}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Substitution in \(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}martingale}\) proves
\[
 E(D_{nb}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
 =w_{nb}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a(\bar R_{nba}-\bar R_{nba})=0,
 \qquad b=1,2.
\]
All variables are integrable because, for fixed \(n\), they take finitely many finite real values.  The tower identity now gives
\[
 E(D_{n1})=E\{E(D_{n1}\mid\mathcal F_{n,0})\}=0.
\]
Moreover, \(D_{n1}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,1}\)-measurable: it is a function of the fixed first-block arrays and the first-block assignment, all of which are known after block one.  Consequently, the pull-out and tower identities for conditional expectation give
\[
 E(D_{n1}D_{n2})
 =E\!\left[D_{n1}E(D_{n2}\mid\mathcal F_{n,1})\right]=0.
\]
Thus no cross-block covariance survives adaptivity.  Finally, setting \(B_n=2\) in the defining formula for predictable quadratic variation in \(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}martingale}\) gives, pathwise,
\[
 V_n=E(D_{n1}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,0})
     +E(D_{n2}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,1}).
\]
Since both increments have mean zero, expansion of the square and the preceding cross-moment calculation also show that the unconditional design variance is
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D_{n1}+D_{n2})
 =E(D_{n1}^2)+E(D_{n2}^2)
 =E\!\left[E(D_{n1}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,0})
             +E(D_{n2}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,1})\right]
 =E(V_n).
\]

Here is the promised exhaustive four-unit check.  Take two arms, four units in each block, first-block counts \((2,2)\), and contrast \(c=(c_1,c_2)\).  Index each first-block assignment by the arm-one subset
\[
 \mathcal S=\{12,13,14,23,24,34\},
\]
each member having probability \(1/6\); its complement receives arm two.  Put \(x_i=R_{n1i}(1)\), \(y_i=R_{n1i}(2)\), \(\bar x=4^{-1}\sum_i x_i\), and \(\bar y=4^{-1}\sum_i y_i\).  On history \(S\in\mathcal S\), the first score is exactly
\[
 d_1(S)=w_{n1}\left[
 c_1\left\{\frac12\sum_{i\in S}x_i-\bar x\right\}
 +c_2\left\{\frac12\sum_{i\notin S}y_i-\bar y\right\}
 \right].
\]
The six assignments form the three complementary pairs \((12,34)\), \((13,24)\), and \((14,23)\).  For each pair, direct subtraction from the four-unit means gives \(d_1(S^c)=-d_1(S)\), so
\[
 \frac16\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}d_1(S)=0,
 \qquad
 q_1:=\operatorname{Var}(D_{n1}\mid\mathcal F_{n,0})
 =\frac16\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}d_1(S)^2.
\]

The quota switch can genuinely depend on outcomes.  For example, choose the fixed first unit so that \(Y_{n1,1}(1)=1\) and \(Y_{n1,1}(2)=-1\), and after block one set
\[
 k(S):=m_{n2,1}
 =\begin{cases}
 1,&Y_{n1,1}^{\mathrm{obs}}>0,\\
 3,&Y_{n1,1}^{\mathrm{obs}}<0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad m_{n2,2}=4-k(S).
\]
This rule is \(\mathcal F_{n,1}\)-measurable and selects \((1,3)\) on the three histories containing unit one in \(S\), and \((3,1)\) on the other three.  Given a first history \(S\), allow the predictable second-block adjustment, and hence the residuals, to depend on that history; write \(u_i(S)=R_{n2i}(1)\), \(v_i(S)=R_{n2i}(2)\), with corresponding four-unit means \(\bar u(S)\) and \(\bar v(S)\).  The four possible arm-one sets are
\[
 \mathcal T_1=\{1,2,3,4\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_3=\{123,124,134,234\},
\]
where the notation lists singleton or three-element subsets.  Each \(T\in\mathcal T_{k(S)}\) has conditional probability \(1/4\), and its score is
\[
 d_2(T;S)=w_{n2}\left[
 c_1\left\{\frac1{k(S)}\sum_{i\in T}u_i(S)-\bar u(S)\right\}
 +c_2\left\{\frac1{4-k(S)}\sum_{i\notin T}v_i(S)-\bar v(S)\right\}
 \right].
\]
Across either list \(\mathcal T_k\), each unit occurs in the arm-one subset in the fraction \(k/4\) of the four assignments and in its complement in the fraction \((4-k)/4\).  Therefore, for every one of the six first-block histories,
\[
 \frac14\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_{k(S)}}d_2(T;S)=0,
 \qquad
 q_2(S):=\operatorname{Var}(D_{n2}\mid\mathcal F_{n,1}=S)
 =\frac14\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_{k(S)}}d_2(T;S)^2.
\]
This enumerates all \(6\times4=24\) adaptive assignment paths.  In particular, the complete cross-block calculation is
\[
 \frac16\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}d_1(S)
 \left\{\frac14\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_{k(S)}}d_2(T;S)\right\}=0.
\]
For every first-block history \(S\), the realized predictable quadratic variation is the sum of the two conditional variances,
\[
 V_n(S)=q_1+q_2(S),
\]
and averaging over the six histories gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D_{n1}+D_{n2})
 =q_1+\frac16\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}q_2(S)=E(V_n).
\]
The calculation conditions only on the prior history \(\mathcal F_{n,0}\) or \(\mathcal F_{n,1}\), never on the realized final adaptive path.

statements.statement: The constructions in \(\text{def:twoarm-sorting}\) equal \(J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(J_{nb}^{+}\) for \(K=2\). For each fixed \(K\), feeding the observable assigned-arm measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)}\) into the finite primal programs in \(\text{def:fixed-k-lp}\) attains \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\), and their Kantorovich duals have the same values. These are exact convexified empirical endpoints. At any single history node, every rational optimal plan is realized by a deterministic fixed-potential-outcome block completion after finite replication of that node's armwise lists, so its LP endpoints are asymptotically nodewise completion-attainable as block sizes grow. No same-size integrality assertion for \(K>2\), and no cross-history assertion that one \(\Xi_n\) realizes independently chosen nodewise plans, is made.
statements.justification: The result turns the abstract envelope into sorting for two arms and a finite auditable computation for multiple arms.

statements.consumer: A four-arm complete-block redesign of the NewbyEtAl2025MentalHealth minitrials can compute each endpoint using a fixed-\(K\) transportation program.
statements.proof_tex:
The two-arm endpoint identities follow from \(\mathrm{lem:twoarm\text{-}rearrangement\text{-}extrema}\).  To display the sign, write
\[
 \frac12(x-y)^2=\frac12x^2+\frac12y^2-xy.
\]
The marginal square terms are fixed, so equal-rank pairing maximizes \(E(XY)\) and minimizes the quadratic cost, while reverse-rank pairing minimizes \(E(XY)\) and maximizes the cost.

For general fixed \(K\), label every atom even when several labels have the same numerical value.  A coupling of the labeled empirical measures assigns a nonnegative mass \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\) to each tuple of labels.  Its \(a\)-th marginal is uniform if and only if
\[
 \sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=m_{nba}^{-1}
\]
for every \(a\) and \(i_a\).  Thus the feasible arrays in \(\mathrm{def:fixed\text{-}k\text{-}lp}\) are exactly the couplings of the observed empirical margins, and its objective is exactly the quadratic transport cost.  Attainment and equality with the finite Kantorovich dual values now follow from \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}discrete\text{-}mot\text{-}duality}\), for both minimization and maximization (apply the minimization result to the negative cost for the latter).

It remains to prove the paper-specific replication assertion.  The constraint matrix and right-hand side of the finite program are rational.  A nonempty bounded rational polytope has a rational optimal extreme point: Gaussian elimination on the active equalities expresses every extreme point using rational arithmetic.  Let \(\pi\) be such an optimum and choose an integer \(L\) divisible by every \(m_{nba}\) and by every denominator of every \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\).  Create \(L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\) replicated units of joint type \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\).  The marginal constraints imply that label \(i_a\) occurs exactly
\[
 \sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}}L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=L/m_{nba}
\]
times.  Hence every armwise list is replicated by the same integral factor, and the empirical joint law of the replicated common unit labels is exactly \(\pi\).  Assigning to each replicated unit the corresponding armwise residual values and then choosing fixed potential outcomes and predictable fitted values with their prescribed difference realizes this plan at that single node.  This construction neither preserves the original unreplicated block size nor enforces compatibility with another history node, which proves exactly the stated boundary.

As an arithmetic stress test, take both centered lists to be \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\).  For the unnormalized contrast \((1,-1)\), equal-rank pairing gives cost \(0\), reverse-rank pairing gives \((4+4+4+4)/4=4\), and therefore \(U_n-L_n=4w_{nb}^2/3>0\) when \(n_{nb}=4\).  The normalized contrast divides both costs and the width by two, exactly as recorded in \(\mathrm{def:pmone\text{-}witness}\).

statements.statement: For every arm and block, form the observable assigned-arm measure \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}}\), centered by the observed assigned-arm residual mean \(\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}\), and feed exactly these measures into \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\) and the plug-in envelope. There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}<\infty\), depending only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\), such that for every \(n\), \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}\left[1\wedge\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\right]\le C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n.\] Consequently, for every \(\eta>0\), \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left(\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}>\eta\right)\le\frac{C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n}{1\wedge\eta}\longrightarrow0.\] The same bound, without the factor two implicit in the displayed sum, holds for the normalized Hausdorff distance between \([\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\) and \([L_n,U_n]\). Probability and expectation are over the original sequential randomization. The inequalities hold uniformly over pre-block histories generated by arrays in the common-parameter class, use observable assigned-arm centering throughout, and do not condition on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\) or freeze the realized final counts.
statements.justification: The explicit common-parameter rate is the missing bridge from oracle partial identification to uniform adaptive inference.

statements.consumer: This theorem permits endpoint reporting during a batched multi-arm trial while preserving unconditional design-based validity.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(r=4+\delta_0\) and condition on an arbitrary realized \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-history.  All quantities below are then finite-population quantities.  For an arm \(a\), write \(X_i=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}\), \(N=n_{nb}\), and \(m=m_{nba}\).  By Jensen's inequality and \(\mathrm{ass:residual\text{-}moments}\),
\[
 \frac1N\sum_i|X_i|^r
 \le 2^{r-1}\left\{\frac1N\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^r+|\bar R_{nba}|^r\right\}
 \le 2^r C_R. \tag{1}
\]
The assigned labels form a simple random sample without replacement of size \(m\) by \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}block\text{-}randomization}\).

We first derive, rather than assume, the finite-population transport bound needed below.  Let \(\nu=m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}\delta_{X_i}\) and \(\mu=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{X_i}\).  Clip both measures to \([-T,T]\), partition that interval into \(H\) cells of length at most \(2T/H\), and project each cell onto one representative.  If \(P_h\) and \(\widehat P_h\) are the population and sample masses of cell \(h\), the exact inclusion probabilities of simple random sampling give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat P_h\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
 =\frac{N-m}{m(N-1)}P_h(1-P_h)\le\frac1{2m},
\]
where \(N\ge2\).  Hence
\[
 E\!\left(\sum_{h=1}^H|\widehat P_h-P_h|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)\le \frac{H}{\sqrt{2m}}. \tag{2}
\]
Couple the common mass within each cell and move unmatched clipped mass by at most \(2T\).  Equations (1)--(2), Markov's inequality applied to \(|X|^r\), and the triangle inequality for quadratic transport give
\[
 E\{W_2^2(\nu,\mu)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
 \le C\left(\frac{T^2}{H^2}+\frac{T^2H}{\sqrt m}+T^{-(r-2)}\right). \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, each clipping leg costs at most
\(N^{-1}\sum_iX_i^2\mathbf 1\{|X_i|>T\}\le 2^rC_RT^{-(r-2)}\), and the expected sample clipping cost equals the population clipping cost by the first-order inclusion probability.

Choose \(H=\lceil m^{1/6}\rceil\) and \(T=m^{1/(3r)}\).  Then every term in (3) is bounded by a constant times
\[
 m^{-\beta},\qquad \beta=\frac{r-2}{3r}. \tag{4}
\]
The actual plug-in margin translates \(\nu\) by minus its sample mean.  Since the population mean of the \(X_i\)'s is zero and simple-random-sampling covariance gives
\[
 E\left[\left\{m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i\right\}^2\middle|\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right]
 =\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2\le C/m,
\]
another triangle inequality preserves (4):
\[
 E\{W_2^2(\widehat\mu_{nba},\mu_{nba})\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}\le C m_{nba}^{-\beta}. \tag{5}
\]

The sample-variance error is controlled directly.  Apply the same inclusion-probability covariance identity to the finite list \(X_i^2\); (1) supplies its second moment.  After expanding the sample variance into the sampled second moment minus the squared sampled mean, and accounting for the factors \(m/(m-1)\) and \(N/(N-1)\), one obtains, for \(m\ge2\),
\[
 E\{|\widehat S_{nba}^2-S_{nba}^2|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}\le C m_{nba}^{-1/2}. \tag{6}
\]
The constant in (1)--(6) depends only on \(\delta_0\) and \(C_R\).

We next derive continuity of both multi-marginal endpoints.  Couple each \(\mu_{nba}\) optimally in quadratic transport to \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\), and glue those armwise kernels to an arbitrary \(\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}\).  If \(X\) has law \(\gamma\) and the resulting \(Y\) has the coupled empirical margins, then \(\mathrm{ass:contrast\text{-}normalization}\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and (1) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |E(c^\top X)^2-E(c^\top Y)^2|
 &\le\{E(c^\top(X-Y))^2\}^{1/2}\{E(c^\top(X+Y))^2\}^{1/2}\\
 &\le\left\{\sum_aW_2^2(\mu_{nba},\widehat\mu_{nba})\right\}^{1/2}
       \left\{2\sum_a(E X_a^2+E Y_a^2)\right\}^{1/2}.
 \end{aligned}\tag{7}
\]
Apply (7) first to an optimizer for the population margins and then in the reverse direction to an optimizer for the empirical margins.  Taking conditional expectations and using (5), the bounded second moments from (1), and fixed \(K\), yields for both signs
\[
 E\{|\widehat J_{nb}^{\pm}-J_{nb}^{\pm}|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
 \le C\left(\min_a m_{nba}\right)^{-\beta/2}. \tag{8}
\]
This argument applies to minima and maxima and does not require uniqueness of a transport plan.

Let \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\), so \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\).  Executed overlap gives \(m_{nba}^{-1}\le(\varepsilon_0n_{nb})^{-1}\), while \((n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\le2n_{nb}^{-1}\).  Combining (6)--(8), summing the absolute block errors, and using the tower property along the original adaptive filtration gives, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{\mathbb D}\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}
 &\le \frac{C}{s_n^2}\sum_bt_{nb}
 \left(q_n^{-1/2}+q_n^{-\beta/2}\right)\\
 &\le Cq_n^{-\kappa},\qquad
 \kappa=\frac{r-2}{6r}.
 \end{aligned}\tag{9}
\]
Nothing in this tower calculation conditions on the terminal history: at block \(b\), the counts and fitted values are merely held fixed at their pre-block values, the conditional bound is uniform in that history, and then that history is integrated out.

Set \(e=\delta_0/[8(4+\delta_0)]\).  Since
\[
 \kappa=\frac{2+\delta_0}{6(4+\delta_0)}>\frac{\delta_0}{8(4+\delta_0)}=e,
\]
and \(\log(2B_nK)>1\), (9), together with the outer truncation by one for the finitely many cases with \(q_n<2\), implies
\[
 \sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}\left[1\wedge
 \frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\right]
 \le C_{\mathrm{ep}}\left\{\frac{\log(2B_nK)}{q_n}\right\}^{e}
 \le C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n.
\]
All constants are common over \(\mathfrak D\) and depend only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\).  If \(X_n\) denotes the nonnegative normalized endpoint error, then
\(\mathbf 1\{X_n>\eta\}\le(1\wedge X_n)/(1\wedge\eta)\), which proves the displayed probability bound.  Finally the Hausdorff distance between two real intervals is
\(\max\{|\widehat L_n-L_n|,|\widehat U_n-U_n|\}\), bounded by the displayed sum, so it obeys the same estimate.  Because \(q_n/\log(2B_nK)\to\infty\) and \(\ell_n\to0\), \(r_n\to0\).

statements.statement: For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), assume in addition that \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}stabilization}\) holds uniformly for the displayed common-parameter class \(\mathfrak D\). Then \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.\] More precisely, the common leverage envelope \(\ell_n\to0\), the common residual-moment envelope \((\delta_0,C_R)\), the finite-population nondegeneracy condition \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\), and uniform predictable-QV stabilization imply \((\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)/\sqrt{V_n}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\) uniformly over \(\mathfrak D\). The exact-envelope theorem gives \(V_n\le U_n\) pathwise, and the explicit bound \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n=o(1)\) permits \(U_n\) to be replaced by \(\widehat U_n\). No conditioning on the terminal adaptive path is required.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix an array \(\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D\), and let all expectations and probabilities below be under its original sequential randomization law.  By \(\text{def:aipw-estimator}\), consistency, and \(p_{nba}=m_{nba}/n_{nb}\), direct subtraction of \(\tau_n\) gives
\[
\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n
=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a
\left\{\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}
\mathbf 1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}\right\}
=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}D_{nb}=M_{nB_n}.
\]
The first equality uses \(Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{nbi}(Z_{nbi})\) from \(\mathrm{ass:consistency\text{-}no\text{-}interference}\), and the second is \(\text{def:block-martingale}\).  The martingale assertion in \(\text{thm:exact-predictable-ot-envelope}\), proved from predictable counts, predictable adjustment, and conditional complete-block randomization, therefore shows that \((D_{nb})_{b\le B_n}\) is a square-integrable martingale-difference array.  In particular, cross-block covariance terms vanish by iterated expectation; no terminal-history conditioning is involved.

We next derive the Lindeberg condition from the primitive moment and leverage assumptions.  Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), put
\[
x_i(a)=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba},\qquad
X_a=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}
\mathbf 1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}x_i(a).
\]
Then \(D_{nb}=w_{nb}\sum_a c_aX_a\).  The residual-moment assumption, the power-mean inequality, and Jensen's inequality imply
\[
\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_i|x_i(a)|^4
\le16\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^4
\le16\left\{\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\right\}^{4/(4+\delta_0)}
\le16C_R^{4/(4+\delta_0)}.
\tag{1}
\]
Here all sums in (1) are over \(i\in\mathcal U_{nb}\); the last inequality is exactly \(\mathrm{ass:residual\text{-}moments}\).

For completeness, the needed fourth-moment sampling bound follows by finite-population algebra.  For any centered list \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\), let \(S\) be a uniformly chosen subset of size \(m\), set \(A_r=\sum_{i=1}^N x_i^r\), and let \(\pi_r=(m)_r/(N)_r\), with \(\pi_r=0\) when \(r>m\).  Expanding the fourth power and using \(\sum_i x_i=0\) yields
\[
E\left(\sum_{i\in S}x_i\right)^4
=\{\pi_1-7\pi_2+12\pi_3-6\pi_4\}A_4
+3\{\pi_2-2\pi_3+\pi_4\}A_2^2.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, the index multiplicity patterns \(4\), \(3+1\), \(2+2\), \(2+1+1\), and \(1+1+1+1\) contribute respectively
\[
\pi_1A_4,\quad -4\pi_2A_4,\quad
3\pi_2(A_2^2-A_4),\quad
6\pi_3(2A_4-A_2^2),\quad
\pi_4(3A_2^2-6A_4),
\]
which proves (2).  Since \(0\le\pi_r\le1\) and \(A_2^2\le NA_4\), if \(m\ge\varepsilon_0N\), then
\[
E\left(\frac1m\sum_{i\in S}x_i\right)^4
\le \left(\frac{26}{\varepsilon_0}+\frac{12}{\varepsilon_0^2}\right)
\frac1{m^2}\frac{A_4}{N}.
\tag{3}
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}block\text{-}randomization}\), the marginal arm-\(a\) sample is precisely such a uniform subset, and \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\) gives \(m_{nba}\ge\varepsilon_0n_{nb}\).  Combining (1)--(3), \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\) from \(\mathrm{ass:contrast\text{-}normalization}\), and
\[
\left(\sum_ac_aX_a\right)^4
\le\left(\sum_aX_a^2\right)^2
\le K\sum_aX_a^4,
\]
gives a constant \(C_0<\infty\), depending only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\), such that
\[
E(D_{nb}^4\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
\le C_0\left(\frac{w_{nb}^2}{n_{nb}}\right)^2
\quad\text{almost surely.}
\tag{4}
\]

Define the deterministic, array-specific scale
\[
\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2=E_{\mathbb D}V_n.
\]
Martingale orthogonality gives \(\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb D}(M_{nB_n})\), while \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}growth}\) gives
\[
\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2\ge v_0s_n^2>0.
\tag{5}
\]
Writing \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\), (4), (5), \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\), and \(\mathrm{ass:block\text{-}leverage}\) give the uniform Lyapunov bound
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\frac{\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E_{\mathbb D}D_{nb}^4}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^4}
\le\frac{C_0}{v_0^2}
\frac{\sum_bt_{nb}^2}{s_n^4}
\le\frac{C_0}{v_0^2}\ell_n\longrightarrow0.
\tag{6}
\]
For every \(\epsilon>0\), define the conditional Lindeberg quantity
\[
\Lambda_{n,\mathbb D}(\epsilon)
=\frac1{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}
E_{\mathbb D}\left[D_{nb}^2\mathbf 1\{|D_{nb}|>\epsilon\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}\}
\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right].
\]
By \(u^2\mathbf 1\{|u|>x\}\le u^4/x^2\), (6), and Markov's inequality,
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}\Lambda_{n,\mathbb D}(\epsilon)
\le\frac1{\epsilon^2}
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\frac{\sum_bE_{\mathbb D}D_{nb}^4}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^4}
\longrightarrow0,
\tag{7}
\]
so the conditional Lindeberg condition holds uniformly in probability.

The added classical martingale central limit theorem \(\text{lem:martingale-clt-predictable-variation}\) applies because (7) supplies its Lindeberg premise and \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}stabilization}\) supplies
\[
\frac{V_n}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2}
=\frac{V_n}{E_{\mathbb D}V_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\text{in probability, uniformly over }\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D.
\tag{8}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}}
=\frac{M_{nB_n}}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)
\quad\text{uniformly over }\mathfrak D.
\tag{9}
\]
To justify the uniform conclusion from the cited pointwise theorem, suppose (9) failed.  Then some subsequence and choices \(\mathbb D_n\in\mathfrak D\) would keep a fixed distributional discrepancy from zero.  The diagonal array \((\mathbb D_n)\) still satisfies (7) and (8), with the same constants and envelopes, so the cited theorem gives convergence along that subsequence, a contradiction.  Combining (8) and (9) by Slutsky's argument, justified by the same diagonal-subsequence device, yields
\[
T_{n,\mathbb D}:=\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)
\quad\text{uniformly over }\mathfrak D.
\tag{10}
\]

It remains to establish conservative studentization.  The pathwise containment in \(\mathrm{thm:exact-predictable-ot-envelope}\) gives \(V_n\le U_n\).  Moreover, \(q_n/\log(2B_nK)\to\infty\), \(\ell_n\to0\), and \(\delta_0>0\) imply directly from the definition of \(r_n\) that \(r_n\to0\).  Therefore \(\mathrm{thm:history-uniform-plugin}\), together with \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\), gives, for each fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{|\widehat U_n-U_n|>\eta V_n\}
\le
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left\{\frac{|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}>\eta v_0\right\}
\le\frac{C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n}{1\wedge(\eta v_0)}
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{11}
\]
On the complementary event in (11),
\[
\widehat U_n\ge U_n-\eta V_n\ge(1-\eta)V_n.
\tag{12}
\]
Let \(A_{n,\mathbb D}(\eta)=\{|\widehat U_n-U_n|\le\eta V_n\}\).  By the definition of \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\) and (12),
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}
\ge
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{|T_{n,\mathbb D}|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\eta}\}
-\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{A_{n,\mathbb D}(\eta)^c\}.
\]
Thus (10), (11), and continuity of the standard normal distribution function \(\Phi\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}
&\ge
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{|T_{n,\mathbb D}|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\eta}\}\\
&=2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\eta}\right)-1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
Letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) in (13) gives \(1-\alpha\), proving the asserted coverage.  The proof uses the deterministic normalization \(E_{\mathbb D}V_n\) separately for each array.  It does not require \(E_{\mathbb D}V_n/s_n^2\) to converge, uniformly or pointwise, to any common scalar, and every probability above is unconditional under the original sequential design.

Let \((D_{nb})_{b\le B_n}\) be a triangular array of square-integrable martingale differences with respect to the pre-increment histories \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), let \(V_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\), and put \(\sigma_n^2=E(V_n)>0\).  If \(V_n/\sigma_n^2\to1\) in probability and, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\frac1{\sigma_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E\left[D_{nb}^2\mathbf 1\{|D_{nb}|>\epsilon\sigma_n\}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right]\to0
\quad\text{in probability},
\]
then \(\sigma_n^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}D_{nb}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\).

For each \(n\), define, within this statement,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A_n&=\sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}
 \frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}\left[
 \inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}}\int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma-J_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi),-}\right],\\
 C_n&=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}\sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}
 \sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}\left[
 \int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}
 -\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}}\int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma\right].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Whenever \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 \max\{A_n,C_n\}\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\le A_n+C_n,
 \qquad
 \Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\le A_n\le B_n\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n).
\]
Consequently, \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\to0\) if and only if \(A_n\to0\) and \(C_n\to0\).  The first condition is the computable root-to-leaf accumulation of the single-node multi-index integrality losses; the second is exactly the additional cross-history compatibility loss from requiring one fixed potential-outcome array, common unit labels, and one predictable fitting rule.  Zero gap alone does not imply the existence of an admissible nondegenerate near-attaining completion sequence, and therefore does not imply the fixed-fraction undercoverage assertion in \(\mathrm{oeq:completion\text{-}sharpness}\).  In particular, if every nodewise centered margin is \(\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\), then \(A_n=C_n=\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}=\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}=0\), but every completion has \(V_n=0\) and hence violates \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}growth}\).

sampling_model.design: The paper restricts attention to sequential complete randomization within blocks: integer arm quotas are chosen from the pre-block history and assignments are then uniform over allocations realizing those quotas. This is implementable by batched platforms that update quotas between batches and enforce minimum cells or capacity caps; it is a restriction of, rather than a condition supplied by, the broader Li--Zhao block-adaptive framework.
sampling_model.units: A triangular array of fixed finite populations partitioned into growing, disjoint blocks.
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed number \(K\) of arms and a prespecified normalized contrast \(c\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every predictable arm fraction obeys the same constant \(\varepsilon_0\) over arrays and histories.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Armwise outcome adjustments are fit from past blocks only and held fixed within the current block. Each plug-in transport margin uses only assigned-arm observations and is centered by that arm's observed residual sample mean; the common nuisance-residual moment envelope is \((\delta_0,C_R)\).
sampling_model.uniformity: The number of arms \(K\), overlap and moment constants, deterministic lower count sequence \(q_n\), leverage envelope \(\ell_n\), and QV lower constant \(v_0\) are common across \(\mathfrak D\).
sampling_model.randomness: The only randomness is sequential treatment assignment; potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.terminal_conditioning: All guarantees are unconditional under the sequential design and use only pre-block conditioning; the realized final adaptive path is never frozen.

tldr: Under the paper's explicit design restriction of predictable integer quotas followed by uniform complete randomization within each growing block, past-only AIPW adjustments make centered block scores a martingale difference array, so cross-block covariance disappears without conditioning on the realized terminal path. The three adaptive contributions are the predictable complete-block transport envelope, its observable history-uniform plug-in theorem with deterministic rate bound \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n\), and conservative martingale Wald inference from the estimated upper endpoint. Supporting computation uses quantile sorting for two arms and a finite transportation program for fixed \(K\), while the worked \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\) validation gives contrast-square costs zero and four by direct substitution. The static two-arm, regression-adjusted, and nonadaptive-stratified reductions are noncontributory validation checks attributed directly to their published sources. Ex ante completion sharpness is not claimed: the open problem separates single-node integrality from cross-history consistency and asks whether fixed-fraction undercoverage can be attained by one completion sequence whose entire induced triangular array remains in the common-overlap, residual-moment, arm-count, leverage, and nondegeneracy inference class.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's adaptive design-based AIPW theory permits arbitrary history-measurable joint block assignment laws with positive marginals and identifies a martingale covariance, but it neither supplies this paper's predictable fixed-count complete-block restriction nor characterizes the resulting sharp residual-coupling range. Sharp transport variance theory treats static complete or stratified randomization and ordinary empirical marginals.
project_justification.niche: Predictable integer quotas followed by uniform complete-block randomization create a random variance target whose nodewise summands are conditionally static coupling problems. Uniform inference requires common deterministic overlap, moment, arm-count, leverage, and QV envelopes. Any completion used to demonstrate failure of a shortened interval must satisfy those same envelopes across the entire triangular array, in addition to linking all history nodes through common fixed potential outcomes and one fitting rule.
project_justification.fill: The three adaptive contributions are the exact predictable complete-block transport envelope, the observable history-uniform endpoint bound \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n\), and unconditional conservative design-based Wald inference from the estimated upper endpoint. The assigned-arm residual construction and finite-\(K\) program provide the computation supporting those claims. Published static reductions are retained only as attributed validation checks. The normalized history-tree gap, its nodewise integrality component, and fixed-fraction undercoverage over ex ante completion sequences that remain inside the full admissible inference class form one open optimization problem.

related_work: Li and Zhao (2026), Section 5, Definition 2, allow an arbitrary history-measurable joint block assignment law with positive unit-level marginals, and Theorem 6 gives the block-adaptive finite-population AIPW covariance, normality, and conservative coverage; Theorem 5 precedes that extension. The predictable integer quotas and uniform complete-block draw used here are an explicit restriction of that broader framework, motivated by batched platforms that update enforceable quotas between blocks, and are not attributed to Li and Zhao. Their covariance sharpening requires residual additivity. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025), equation (1) and Theorem 1, turn a multi-arm contrast variance into a static quadratic multi-marginal transport problem and control its plug-in value; they do not impose cross-history compatibility on one fixed potential-outcome array. Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014), Lemma 1, Proposition 1, and Corollary 1, provide the two-arm sorting and static sharp-inference prototype without a history tree. Yu, Zhu, and Liu (2025) aggregate two-arm rearrangement bounds over nonadaptive strata and prove consistency in growing-strata regimes. Mikhaeil and Green (2024) show that regression residuals are the correct coupling object for adjusted estimators under nonadaptive two-arm designs. The corresponding static reductions are used only as noncontributory validation benchmarks and are attributed to these papers rather than stated as new results. Ober-Reynolds (2023) obtains directional endpoint limit theory from iid empirical processes. Saco (2026), Assumption 5.11, imposes a high-probability linear lower bound on predictable quadratic variation under iid arrivals, while Theorem 5.14 studentizes by realized quadratic variation; neither result supplies the common finite-population predictable-QV envelope imposed uniformly here. Harshaw, Middleton, and Savje (2026) optimize admissible quadratic bounds under arbitrary designs and separate admissibility from marginal sharpness. Newby et al. (2025) supply the four-arm mental-health consumer, but their participant-level contextual bandit has no minimum or maximum arm allocation and does not implement the fixed-count design; a predictably batched complete-block redesign is required before the main theorem applies.
technical_internal_limitation: The rectangular relaxation permits an independent convexified coupling at each possible history node. Theorems establish sharpness only inside each node's convexified set. The diagnostic \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) isolates failure of a same-size deterministic multi-index matching at one node, whereas \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) also charges the cross-history loss from common unit labels, fixed potential outcomes, and one predictable fitting rule. No theorem asserts that either gap vanishes. Any fixed-fraction undercoverage construction must be one ex ante completion sequence whose induced triangular experiment-analysis array belongs to \(\mathfrak D\); nodewise compatibility alone is insufficient. Noncontributory validation appendix: direct substitution of the centered lists \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\) into the two-arm costs gives \(J_{nb}^{-}=0\) from equal-rank pairing and \(J_{nb}^{+}=4\) from reverse-rank pairing for the unnormalized contrast \((1,-1)\); with \(n_{nb}=4\), the envelope width is \(4w_{nb}^2/3\). When \(B_n=1\), \(K=2\), \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), and \(c\) is proportional to \((1,-1)\), direct substitution in the definitions recovers the Aronow--Green--Lee rearrangement envelope, plug-in endpoint, and conservative Wald interval after normalization. Allowing an arbitrary pre-randomization adjustment in that one-block two-arm calculation recovers the Mikhaeil--Green residual envelope. Making counts and adjustments history-independent reduces the endpoint sum to the nonadaptive stratified aggregation of Yu--Zhu--Liu. These three reductions are published sanity checks, not proposal results.
honest_scope: The three adaptive contributions are the exact predictable complete-block transport envelope, the observable history-uniform plug-in theorem, and conservative martingale coverage using the estimated transport upper endpoint. The two-block covariance enumeration, two-arm sorting, and fixed-\(K\) LP are supporting results. Predictable integer quotas followed by uniform complete-block randomization are an explicit paper design restriction, justified by batched quota-controlled platforms and not attributed to Li and Zhao's broader assignment model. The \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\) arithmetic and the Aronow--Green--Lee, Mikhaeil--Green, and Yu--Zhu--Liu static reductions are noncontributory validation checks, not to-prove results. The QV lower envelope is a nonstandard finite-population paper assumption; Saco (2026), Assumption 5.11, instead uses a high-probability linear predictable-QV lower bound and Theorem 5.14 studentizes by realized QV. No ex ante completion-sharpness claim is made. Open-ended Question 6 separates \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) from cross-history consistency and permits a fixed-fraction undercoverage conclusion only for one ex ante completion sequence whose full induced triangular array belongs to \(\mathfrak D\), so the common overlap, count, leverage, residual-moment, plug-in, QV, and martingale-CLT requirements all apply. The published Newby et al. allocation is a participant-level contextual bandit rather than complete-block randomization; the paper is a consumer for a predictably batched redesign, not a claim of immediate reanalysis.
